prompt: Put the road of a push message in order.
items: the push service on the phone
the notification shade, or your app

prompt: Why can the planner's server not send a message straight to the student's phone?

choices.text: Phones refuse connections from servers outside the store
choices.why: No such rule; the obstacle is reaching the phone at all.

choices.text: Push messages must be encrypted by Google or Apple
choices.why: Encryption is not the reason the road goes through them.

choices.text: It has no fixed address, sleeps and changes networks
choices.why: Right. Only the platform's service keeps a connection to it, shared by every app.

choices.text: The server would need the student's phone number
choices.why: Push has nothing to do with phone numbers.

prompt: According to Apple's documentation, when does APNs issue a new device token? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: When the device is restored from a backup
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: When the app is installed on a new device
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: When the operating system is reinstalled
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Every time a notification is delivered
choices.why: Delivering a message does not change the address it was delivered to.

prompt: The planner saved its device token on first launch and never sends it again. What happens after the student restores her phone from a backup?

choices.text: Pushes stop, with no error on the phone
choices.why: Right. The server keeps addressing a token that is no longer hers.

choices.text: The app crashes on launch
choices.why: Nothing on the phone fails; the server just addresses the old token.

choices.text: Pushes keep arriving, because a token is permanent
choices.why: Restoring from a backup issues a new token.

choices.text: Apple forwards messages from the old token to the new one
choices.why: There is no forwarding; the app has to send the new token.

prompt: APNs holds messages for an offline phone. How many of the planner's notifications does it keep?

choices.text: None: APNs only delivers to phones that are online
choices.why: It stores one and delivers it when the phone is back.

choices.text: All of them, for 30 days
choices.why: Up to 30 days, but only one.

choices.text: The last four, one per collapse key
choices.why: Collapse keys are FCM's; APNs keeps one per app.

choices.text: One, in most cases the latest
choices.why: Right. Apple's documentation says it stores only one notification per app.

prompt: When an app is uninstalled, Expo's push service answers a message to its token with the error ___, and the server should stop sending to it.
The planner is not on screen and a notification message arrives with a title and a body. What shows it?

choices.text: The planner, which the system starts to draw it
choices.why: The system shows it without starting the app.

choices.text: The system
choices.why: Right. Your code runs when the person taps it.

choices.text: Nothing, until the planner is opened
choices.why: That would make reminders useless; the system shows it at once.

choices.text: The FCM or APNs app installed on the phone
choices.why: There is no such app; it is the system's push service.

prompt: What is the maximum payload, in bytes, of an ordinary (not VoIP) remote notification, according to Apple?
Why is a data-only message the wrong way to make sure the week refreshes?

choices.text: It is larger than a notification message
choices.why: Size is not the problem; both have the same limit.

choices.text: The system does not guarantee to hand it to the app
choices.why: Right. Doze, or too many of them, and the app never sees it.

choices.text: Only iOS supports it
choices.why: Android has data messages too.

choices.text: It shows a notification the student did not ask for
choices.why: A data-only message shows nothing.

prompt: payload.ts refused the message that carried the whole week. What should the server send instead?

choices.text: The week, split into two pushes of half the size
choices.why: Two pushes can collapse into one or arrive out of order.

choices.text: Nothing: the student opens the app anyway
choices.why: A short push still makes the refresh happen sooner.

choices.text: The week compressed, so it fits
choices.why: Even when it fits, the push can be late or lost; the data belongs on the server.

choices.text: The id of what changed; the app fetches the rest
choices.why: Right. A push is a doorbell, not a parcel.

prompt: Match each part of the reminder to where FCM's HTTP v1 message puts it.
How many bytes did the FCM message for the s3 reminder measure?
A reminder says 'Sessão de Programação às 19h' and measures 98 characters. Why does payload.ts count with Buffer.byteLength rather than .length?

choices.text: The limit is in bytes, and each accented letter is two bytes in UTF-8
choices.why: Right. Characters undercount the bytes a service sees.

choices.text: Buffer.byteLength is faster
choices.why: Speed is not why; correctness is.

choices.text: .length counts the JSON's quotes twice
choices.why: It counts each quote once; that is not the difference.

choices.text: FCM counts in UTF-16, which .length does not
choices.why: JavaScript's .length is the UTF-16 count; the limit is in bytes of UTF-8 JSON.

prompt: What does a local notification need that a push does not?

choices.text: A device token
choices.why: That is the push's address; a local notification needs none.

choices.text: A network connection at the moment it fires
choices.why: It fires with no network at all.

choices.text: Nothing beyond the app knowing when
choices.why: Right. The phone's own system keeps the appointment.

choices.text: The app to be running when it fires
choices.why: The system shows it whether or not the app runs.

prompt: The student moves session s3 from Friday to Saturday. What must the app do with the reminder it scheduled?

choices.text: Cancel remind-s3 by its identifier and schedule a new one
choices.why: Right. Otherwise Friday's reminder fires for a session that is no longer there.

choices.text: Nothing: the system notices the session moved
choices.why: The system knows the trigger, not the planner's sessions.

choices.text: Schedule a second reminder for Saturday and leave the first
choices.why: Then she is reminded on Friday of nothing.

choices.text: Ask the server to send a push on Saturday instead
choices.why: A local reminder needs no server, and the old one still fires.

prompt: Why does reminders.ts convert São Paulo wall-clock times with the Intl API rather than subtracting three hours?

choices.text: Because three hours is the wrong offset for São Paulo in October
choices.why: It is right this week; the point is that a fixed number is a rule written by hand.

choices.text: Because Date cannot subtract hours
choices.why: It can; the arithmetic is not the problem.

choices.text: Intl carries each zone's rules, including summer time where it exists
choices.why: Right. A fixed offset is wrong in any city with summer time.

choices.text: Because the phone's clock is in UTC
choices.why: The instant is UTC everywhere; the question is the wall-clock time.

prompt: Run at noon on Wednesday 21 October, how many of the six sessions got a reminder?
Session s3 starts at 19:00 São Paulo time, so its reminder is at 18:45 there, which is ___:45 UTC.
A student installs the planner on an Android 14 phone. Before the app asks for anything, are its notifications on?

choices.text: Yes, until she turns them off
choices.why: From Android 13, a new install starts with them off.

choices.text: No
choices.why: Right. POST_NOTIFICATIONS has to be asked for and granted first.

choices.text: Only for the reminders channel
choices.why: No channel is on before the permission.

choices.text: Only while the app is open
choices.why: The permission is not about the app being open.

prompt: When does Apple's documentation suggest a task app should ask to send reminder notifications?

choices.text: On first launch, before anything else
choices.why: That is the moment it advises against: nobody can see what they are for yet.

choices.text: Every launch until the person agrees
choices.why: The system asks once and records the answer; later requests show nothing.

choices.text: Only after a week of use
choices.why: Apple ties it to the task, not to a number of days.

choices.text: After the person schedules a first task
choices.why: Right. Then the purpose of a reminder is plain.

prompt: What does provisional authorisation on iOS do?

choices.text: Shows the permission prompt again later
choices.why: It shows no prompt at all.

choices.text: Lets the app send loud alerts for a trial week
choices.why: The trial is quiet, not loud.

choices.text: Delivers quietly to Notification Centre, with Keep and Turn Off buttons
choices.why: Right. The person decides having seen one.

choices.text: Allows marketing pushes without opt-in
choices.why: Guideline 4.5.4 still needs an explicit opt-in.

prompt: A student finds 'Shared courses' notifications noisy but wants session reminders. Which design lets her keep one and drop the other on Android?

choices.text: A channel for each kind of message
choices.why: Right. The user controls each channel, and the app cannot change them back.

choices.text: One channel, with a setting inside the app
choices.why: It works only while the app honours it; the system's own control is per channel.

choices.text: Raising the importance of the reminders channel
choices.why: After creation the app cannot change a channel's behaviour.

choices.text: Asking for POST_NOTIFICATIONS twice
choices.why: The permission is for all channels at once.

prompt: Under guideline 4.5.4, which of these may the planner send without anything more? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A reminder before a session the student planned
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: 'Ana shared a course with you'
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: 'New course: 30% off this weekend'
choices.why: Marketing: it needs an explicit opt-in in the app, and a way out.

choices.text: The student's exam marks on the lock screen
choices.why: Sensitive personal information does not go in a push.

prompt: A team wants the planner to remind students 15 minutes before each session. Which design does this lesson point to?

choices.text: A server job that sends a push to every student at the right time
choices.why: It works, but a push can be late or lost, and it needs a token kept fresh.

choices.text: A background task scheduled for 15 minutes before
choices.why: No background mechanism runs at a set time.

choices.text: A data-only push that wakes the app to show the reminder
choices.why: The least reliable kind, for the one message that must be on time.

choices.text: Local notifications, rescheduled whenever the plan changes
choices.why: Right. No server, no network, and the system keeps the time.
